paraphrases.title: 60 mm fan to heatsink duct
paraphrases.request: Duct from a 60 x 60 x 25 mm fan (mounting holes on a 50 mm square pitch) to a 50 x 20 mm heatsink, 30 mm tall. Fan on top, blowing straight down; heatsink below with fins vertical, so its leading face is the 50 x 20 mm top face, where the duct meets it. Smoothly changing section from fan to heatsink; air enters the fins with side seals of 1 mm at most (the outlet slips over the top of the heatsink, gap to its sides between 0.2 and 1 mm). Four M4 socket-head bolts hold the fan through its holes into the duct; all four screws must be reachable with a hex driver from above. One printed FDM duct in PLA, no supports, wall at least 1.6 mm.
paraphrases.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, all from requirements.md section 3: airflow vertical, fan above, heatsink's leading face = its top face (A1); the heatsink modelled as a solid 50 x 20 x 30 box (A2); '1 mm side seals' = a gap of 0.2 to 1 mm round the heatsink's sides under a sleeve (A3); M4 bolts into printed pilots (A5); 'from above' = a straight column along each bolt axis (A6); wall at least 1.6, FDM, no supports (A7, A8).

l1.text: Place the 60 x 60 x 25 mm fan with airflow straight down, the 50 x 20 x 30 mm heatsink below it with its 50 x 20 mm top face as the leading face, and four M4 bolts, all from the parts catalogue. Fan axis within 1.0 mm of the heatsink face centre, no colliding parts. Declare that layout.
The duct flange sits flat on the fan's exhaust face (60 x 60 mm outline within 1 mm, at least 800 mm² of contact) with four screw pilots on the fan's 50 mm square hole pattern.
The inlet opening is nearly as large as the fan's air bore: inscribed circle at least 54 mm, area at least 85% of the bore (and at most the bore plus 1 mm).

Smooth change from fan opening to heatsink face: the passage narrows steadily, no steps; walls slope no more than 45 degrees from the air direction; cross-section area changes by no more than 10% per millimetre of height and never falls below 950 mm²; the transition is 18 to 34 mm long.
The passage ends exactly at the heatsink leading face; the outlet opening covers the whole 50 x 20 mm face so all the air enters the fins, and is no bigger than 52 x 22 mm.
The outlet slips over the top of the heatsink as a sleeve, with a gap of 0.2 to 1.0 mm to each of its four sides over at least 5 mm of overlap.
Nothing printed enters the fan or the heatsink; nothing blocks the fan intake: the 58 mm bore column above the intake face is free for 15 mm.
Four M4 socket-head bolts hold the fan through its holes into pilot holes in the flange (3.1 to 3.5 mm diameter, at least 6 mm deep); each engages at least 5 mm and stops clear of the pilot end.
Test: a hex driver reaches every fan screw head from straight above; a 6 mm column 25 mm long along each bolt axis is clear.
The duct is airtight except for its inlet and outlet; walls at least 1.6 mm thick.
Prints on FDM without supports in the stated print orientation: no overhang steeper than 45° from vertical, no bridge over 15 mm, at least 25% and 800 mm² on the bed.
Printed duct max 64 x 64 x 45 mm, symmetric about the fan axis within 1 mm.
Deliver the duct STL (in the declared layout frame), OpenSCAD source, declared layout, print orientation and the agent's own clearance report; the report must agree with an independent measurement.

paraphrases.title: 60 mm fan to heatsink duct
paraphrases.request: I need a printed duct linking a fan, 60 x 60 x 25 mm with mounting holes on a 50 mm square pitch, to a heatsink measuring 50 x 20 mm and 30 mm in height. The fan is mounted above and blows straight downward onto the heatsink, whose fins run vertically; the leading face is therefore the heatsink's 50 x 20 mm top, and that is where the duct ends. The section should change smoothly from fan to heatsink, and the duct's outlet fits as a sleeve over the heatsink top, leaving 0.2 to 1 mm between it and the sides, so the side seals are no more than 1 mm. The fan is bolted down with four M4 socket-head bolts through its holes into the duct, and a hex driver has to reach all four screws from above. FDM, PLA, no supports, one part, wall of 1.6 mm minimum.
paraphrases.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, all from requirements.md section 3: airflow vertical, fan above, heatsink's leading face = its top face (A1); the heatsink modelled as a solid 50 x 20 x 30 box (A2); '1 mm side seals' = a gap of 0.2 to 1 mm round the heatsink's sides under a sleeve (A3); M4 bolts into printed pilots (A5); 'from above' = a straight column along each bolt axis (A6); wall at least 1.6, FDM, no supports (A7, A8).

l1.text: Declare a layout from the parts catalogue: the 60 x 60 x 25 mm fan blowing straight down, the 50 x 20 x 30 mm heatsink beneath it with its 50 x 20 mm top as the leading face, and four M4 bolts. The fan axis must be within 1.0 mm of the centre of the heatsink face and no parts may collide.

The duct needs a flange lying flat against the fan's exhaust face, with its 60 x 60 mm outline within 1 mm and 800 mm² or more of contact, and four screw pilots laid out on the fan's 50 mm square hole pattern.
The duct inlet should almost match the fan's air bore: its inscribed circle is 54 mm or more, its area at least 85% of the bore and no larger than the bore plus 1 mm.

Going from the fan opening to the heatsink face the passage must narrow steadily with no steps. Wall slope is capped at 45 degrees from the air direction, cross-section area must not drop under 950 mm² nor change faster than 10% per millimetre of height, and the transition is 18 to 34 mm long.
The passage must stop right at the heatsink's leading face, and the outlet opening has to cover that entire 50 x 20 mm face so that all the air goes into the fins, while staying within 52 x 22 mm.
As a sleeve the outlet goes over the heatsink top, with 0.2 mm minimum and 1.0 mm maximum clearance to each of the four sides of the heatsink, over an overlap of 5 mm or more.
No printed material may intrude into the fan or the heatsink or obstruct the fan's intake, so the 58 mm bore column over the intake face stays clear for 15 mm.

The fan is held by four M4 socket-head bolts that pass through its holes and into flange pilot holes of 3.1 to 3.5 mm diameter and 6 mm minimum depth. Every bolt engages 5 mm or more and ends short of the pilot's bottom.
From directly above, a hex driver must get to each fan screw head unobstructed, meaning the 6 mm wide, 25 mm long column along every bolt axis is free.
Apart from the inlet and the outlet the duct must be sealed against air leaks, and its wall thickness is 1.6 mm or more.

Using the print orientation stated in the design, the duct must print on an FDM printer with no supports: overhangs no steeper than 45° from vertical, bridges of 15 mm or less, and a bed contact area of at least 25% (and 800 mm²).
The duct should fit in 64 x 64 x 45 mm and be symmetrical about the fan axis to within 1 mm.

Provide the duct STL in the declared layout frame, the OpenSCAD source, the layout declaration, the print orientation and the agent's own clearance report, which must agree with an independent measurement.
